pebbling_general_foundations.scope: UNBOUNDED theorems: time-reversal symmetry of the reversible pebble game (legal_reverse, exec_reverse_cancel, maxOnes_reverse) and full correctness of Bennett's binary schedule (bennett_general) yielding the achievability half of the reach characterisation: for every p >= 1 a chain of length 2^(p-1) is cleanly reachable with peak p (reach_two_pow). Toward the general impossibility half (Knill Thm 2.3): prefix coverage, roundtrip completeness, and the UNCONDITIONAL restriction lemmas (roadmap step (c)): legality/execution/coverage all commute with restriction to the cells above x (shiftAbove: moves > x re-indexed, x+1 becomes the free left end) and below x (keepBelow), plus the pebble-count split ones = ones(take) + ones(drop). COMPLETED (d)-(f): middle-vertex induction (complete_bound: a complete computation with peak P covers at most 2^P - 1 cells) and the clean-reach corollary (reach_impossible_general: v+1 <= 2^(p-1)). With reach_two_pow this machine-checks the EXACT characterisation reach(p) = 2^(p-1) of Knill 1995 Thm 2.3, both halves fully general

growth_rate_real.scope: UNBOUNDED, but RELATIVE TO submultiplicativity (`Submult`, Lemma 1 of the letter), which is carried as an explicit hypothesis and is not yet formalised in general.  Puts the growth rate c into Lean as a real number: a_k = log f_{k+1} is subadditive, so mathlib's Fekete lemma applies and c := exp(Subadditive.lim).  `growth_le` is the lim = inf phenomenon (c <= f_{m+1}^{1/m} for every finite m); `growth_le_ratio` turns an integer witness f_{m+1} * q^m <= p^m into c <= p/q, which is the form the artifact's witnesses take.  `growth_le_2_6106` instantiates this at m = 59 with rle_f_60 and c_le_2_6106_witness, so the published bound c <= 2.6106 is now a statement about a real number in Lean rather than a step taken on paper.  `growth_le_of_geometric` is the analytic half of the closed-form route: an envelope f_p <= C * B^p gives c <= B, the constant washing out in the Fekete quotient.  Its Nat-side input (M_S = sum of midpoints, f_S <= 2^S M_S) is not yet general, so c <= 2*sqrt 2 is not yet assembled.

lift_above_primitive.scope: UNBOUNDED, route beta (game-side).  Knill's Thm 2.1 has an asymmetric proof: the `<=` half (LAUR-95-2258 p.5) is a construction composing S1 (reach m with S), S3 (reach n-m from m with S-1) and reversed S2 (unreach m with S-1); the `>=` half decomposes an optimal solution matrix.  The construction needs a play on a short chain LIFTED onto the segment above an already-pebbled foundation.  PebblingFoundations has only the projection shiftAbove; this file supplies the lift and its execution law (above the cut a lifted play does what the original does) and foundation law (below the cut nothing changes, so the foundation survives).  The legality and peak laws, and hence the composition itself, are NOT yet proved.

knill_recursion_uniqueness.scope: UNBOUNDED: Knill's recursion has a unique solution.  The structure theorems of this artifact are statements about the generator `gen`/`rowIter`; the bridge to the pebble game has two links, (1) game -> recursion (Knill 1995 Thm 2.1, checked here only on a grid by knill_recursion_agrees_with_game / knillA_agrees_with_F, where `F` is a lookup into a fixed 64x24 table and hence bounded by construction) and (2) recursion -> generator.  Link (2) is proved here in FULL GENERALITY: `solves_unique` shows any two solutions agree on the whole reach range (strong induction on n; a split n = k+l+2 refers back only to l+1 <= n-1), and `solves_eq_gen` identifies every solution with the generated row.  Kernel axioms only, no native_decide.

difference_merge_property_general_core.scope: FULL GENERAL difference-merge property: exchange principle for sorted streams (merged prefix sums = min-split DP value, both directions), multiset preservation, sortedness, PLUS the self-referential closure: generator gen with accumulator-resolved B-stream, invariant (sortedness/bounds), count identity, representation form gen_merge_rep (row = 1 :: smerge prev B) and Knill identity form gen_satisfies_knill for every sorted positive input row.

rle_pebble_values.scope: run-length (RLE) row generator formalised; agreement with the Array DP on S <= 8; exact space-optimal costs f_S certified by native_decide up to S = 60 (f_50 = 328129268250340571627, f_60 = 3864271883997196147394945; the f_60 theorem costs 384 s / 3.2 GB and deliberately exceeds the usual per-theorem budget because it is the witness behind the published bound c <= 2.6106). count_recursion_general.scope: FULLY GENERAL, no hypotheses beyond the seed row [1]: for the canonical generated row sequence rowIter (S = s+2), pointwise domination delta(i,S) <= delta(i,S-1) (via the new superset-order tool smerge_getElem_le_left), the value-counting recursion in BOTH directions (upper C_S(v) <= 1 + C_{S-1}(v) + C_S(v/2), lower C_S(v) >= 1 + C_{S-1}(v) + C_{S-1}(v/2) -- the P_k >= 0 tool), the count(1) law C_S(1) = S-1, and the Pascal binomial bound C_S(2^k) <= 2 C(S+k-1, k+1) - 1.  This machine-checks the combinatorial core of the lower bound c >= 2^{1+eps*} ~ 2.4518; only the analytic entropy step remains outside. ALSO the dual chain: the Knill partial-sum LOWER bound C_S(2^k)+1 >= psum(S-1,k+1) (P_k >= 0, fully general), the binomial median 2^n <= 2 psum(n, m) for n <= 2m+1 (reflection identity, no analysis), and the midpoint bound m_S <= 2^{(S-2)/2} (midpoint_bound_general) -- the combinatorial core of the closed-form upper bound c <= 2 sqrt(2). PLUS the two-split self-referential lower recursion count_recursion_split: C_S(u+w) >= 1 + C_{S-1}(u+w) + min(C_{S-1}(u), C_S(w)) for every split -- its DP fixed point has midpoint exponent ~0.337 vs true log2(d) ~0.3355 (candidate exact characterisation of d; numerics in m1_improved_recursion.py). PLUS the min-max DUAL upper recursion count_recursion_minmax (M8): C_S(v) <= 1 + C_{S-1}(v) + max(C_S(tau), C_{S-1}(v-1-tau)) for every threshold tau, via the prefix structure of the B-column -- captures the E-band within 6e-4 when minimised over tau; the dual DP pair pinches the midpoint two-sidedly with both exponents near log2(d).

composition_anchor.scope: GENERAL composition theorem (追記42): scale covariance of count_recursion_split transports any certificate function L obeying the pure split-recursion laws to scale m_S with mass factor 2^s, the +1s of the recursion exactly absorbing the -1 of the base count: 2^s L(t,v) <= C_{S+t}(m_S v) + 1 (count_composition).  Hence a finite DP certificate L(t,v*) >= 2^t forces the unconditional midpoint bound m_{S+t} <= m_S v* for EVERY S (midpoint_composition), giving c = 2d <= 2 (v*)^{1/t}.  Bounded instance fully in Lean: exact integer DP table t <= 8, v <= 44 re-verified against its defining laws by native_decide, certificate L(8,44) = 256 = 2^8, yielding midpoint_anchor_44: m_{S+8} <= 44 m_S for every S.  Large anchors (T0 = 200: v* = 7157336700599306027008, c <= 2.5788) are Python-certified exact bigint DP (scripts/m5_exact_anchor.py in the paper repo); their Lean replay is future work.

minimax_duality.scope: ZERO DUALITY GAP (追記49): the maximin lower recursion count_recursion_split and the minimax dual upper recursion count_recursion_minmax are EXACT -- identically, not asymptotically.  Core is an elementary duality identity for ANY monotone f, g : Nat -> Nat vanishing at 0: max_{u+w=v} min(f u, g w) = min_{a+b=v-1} max(g a, f b) (weak_duality: pigeonhole; strong_duality_at: crossing-point construction; minimax_duality: both).  The v-1 shift on the minimax side is exactly what closes the discrete gap.  Applied with f = C_{S-1}, g = C_S and the two proven recursions: C_S(v) = 1 + C_{S-1}(v) + max_{u+w=v} min(C_{S-1}(u), C_S(w)) (count_recursion_split_exact), dually with min-max (count_recursion_minmax_exact), and the B-count equals the best split min (bcount_maximin_exact) -- the dual DP pair is ONE exact self-referential recursion, so the two crossing exponents coincide identically (the measured 0.336 vs 0.331 split was grid rounding).  Bounded numeric confirmation: zero gap at all integer v, S <= 30 (scripts/m9_dual_gap.py in the paper repo); in-file native_decide checks at s = 4, 7.

dispersion_bound.scope: DISPERSION LOWER BOUNDS (追記50/52): power-mode supersolutions of the exact minimax recursion.  q = 1 instance lambda = 13/8, threshold tau = floor(3v/8), A = 64: dispersion_main 8^s C_S(v) <= 64 v 13^s unconditionally; at the midpoint (countLe_midv) this inverts to 16^s <= 64 midv(s) 13^s + 8^s, certifying c = 2d >= 32/13 ~ 2.4615 -- the first machine-checked improvement over the entropy bound 2^{1+eps*} ~ 2.4518.  q = 3/2 instance sigma = 9/8 (rho = 81/64, lambda = 729/512), threshold floor(4v/9), integralised via W v = isqrt(10^6 v^3) = floor(1000 v^{3/2}): dispersion32_main 512^s C_S(v) <= W(v) 729^s, midpoint corollary certifying c >= 2^{5/3} * 64/81 ~ 2.5085; refined sigma = 11231/10000 (DispersionBound32b, W' = floor(10^5 v^{3/2})) certifying c >= 2^{5/3} 10^8/11231^2 ~ 2.5169802, within 6e-5 of the q=3/2 optimum 2.5170378; and at the critical sigma = 112308717/10^8 (DispersionBound32c, W' = floor(10^8 v^{3/2}), threshold floor(222162090806 v / 502380643653)) certifying c >= 2^{5/3} 10^16/112308717^2 = 2.5170377412, i.e. within 3.4e-8 of that optimum -- at q = 3/2 the rational rounding of rho now costs essentially nothing, and the whole remaining 2.7e-5 shortfall to 2^{1+kappa*} is the choice of q itself (q* = 1.5153832...).  That last loss is removed by DispersionBound4731, which moves the whole argument to q = 47/31 (the convergent of q* within 7.5e-4 of it): the potential v^{47/31} is integralised by the integer 31st root of RevPebbling.IntRoot, W v = iroot 31 (10^248 v^47) = floor(10^8 v^{47/31}), with s = 1007357123/10^9, D = 10^423, threshold floor(2894171759 v / 6526721862), certifying c >= 2^{1+31/47} 10^279 / 1007357123^31 = 2.5170647241 -- within 1.1e-7 of 2^{1+kappa*}, i.e. the rational dispersion family now matches the conjectured exact value to eight decimals.  The lambda-admissibility conditions are the exact rational dispersion inequalities (272 <= 273 golden-ratio form; 729^2 64^3 <= 145^3 217^2).  Per the Clairaut/envelope analysis (追記52) the supremum of this certified family, c = 2^{1+kappa*} = 2.517065..., is conjecturally the exact growth rate.

crossing_concentration.scope: CROSSING LEMMAS (追記55): the argmax split of the exact maximin bcount_S(v) sits at the crossing crossPeb of the two monotone arms, with bcount = max(C_{S-1}(c), C_S(v-1-c)) (bcount_eq_max_cross) and one-atom sandwiches C_{S-1}(c) <= bcount <= C_{S-1}(c+1), C_S(v-1-c) <= bcount <= C_S(v-c) (bcount_cross_sandwich); the crossing is at or above the midpoint, v/2 <= crossPeb (half_le_crossPeb, via amplification), and strictly below v (crossPeb_lt).  Gives the computable-optimum exact recursion count_recursion_cross_exact and shows the classical floor(v/2) lower recursion is the u = floor(v/2) shadow of the crossing (count_recursion_lower_via_cross).  These are the unconditional inputs of the balanced-concentration reduction (H3 <= H1 + atom condition) in the Clairaut/envelope program.

ratio_convergence_phase01.scope: GENERAL, real-free and subtraction-free: for any positive integer sequence, eventual log-concavity f(p+2)f(p) <= f(p+1)^2 (p >= p0) implies the ratio sequence f(p+1)/f(p) is Cauchy (cross-multiplied predicate; telescoping monotonicity + Archimedean descent, no completeness).  Reduces convergence of the space-optimal ratio to the single measured inequality family G_{p+1} f_{p-1} <= G_p f_p (p >= 15), margin 1-O(1/p).

seam_identity_core.scope: FULL GENERAL combinatorial core of the uniform bound on the supermultiplicativity loss eps (this work, notes 追記67/68): the SEAM IDENTITY N_t(b) = N_{t-1}(b) + beta_t(b) + 1 from the merge representation (making the eps recursion an exact convex combination), the RANK LEMMA (entries below the value at index i number at most i), and the CONSTANT-RUN LEMMA (a constant B-stream block forces both components constant, upgrading Phat <= beta to Phat <= beta - m_B + 1), plus the cleared-denominator margin bound X >= 1 - 1/P_t(b) and the cleared ε-induction step eps_step that yield eps < 3/5 and hence Fekete existence of the profile g(beta).  All statements universally quantified over sorted lists; no native_decide.  eps_step/eps_step_boundary are over the rationals via mathlib; the combinatorial lemmas need only core/Std.  Also the WITNESS LEMMA cle_zipWith_ge_min (a sorted merged-sum stream has at least min(N_l1(u), N_l2(w)) entries <= u+w), which is what lower-bounds beta_{S+t}(ab) in the composition induction, both branches of that induction as arithmetic implications over the rationals, and THE CLOSED INDUCTION itself: eps is defined by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic order (t, b) (terminating by c1 < b), its DP equations are recovered from the definition, and supermult_closed gives N_S(a) N_t(b) (1 - eps) <= N_{S+t}(ab) for all t >= 2 from the row-level inputs.

front_dp_subsolution_framework.scope: FULL GENERAL combinatorial backbone of the four-zone subsolution architecture for the missing upper bound FrontExp(L) <= kappa* (notes 追記76/77): the autonomous front DP L defined by well-founded recursion on lex (t,v) with the implicit same-row term, the split lower bound, the ceiling L <= 2^(t-2), ZONE 0 fully proved (binomial Pascal subsolution sum C(t-2,i) <= L t 2^k via the halving split), and the TRANSFER PRINCIPLE subsolution_le: a rational profile with a verified base row and the one-step property is dominated by L for all t >= T_b.  The analytic Zones I/II supply the one-step hypothesis; the base row is the m30 machine check (0 violations / 98047).  ChordDeficit adds the ALGEBRAIC CORE of Zone I: the dispersion exponent f is only M-semiconcave (f'' > 0 for q > 0.5), so Jensen runs the wrong way and the chord deficit (M/2) w1 w2 (q1-q2)^2 must be carried; chord_deficit derives it from concavity of f - (M/2)q^2, and ledger / ledger_pos assemble Lemma A of the one-step appendix from that plus the two branch gaps, reducing the analytic side to explicit hypotheses on f, E and the soft-plus cap.  Profile.lean machine-checks the paper's profile theorem from supermultiplicativity: in the logarithmic form (Superadd, joint superadditivity with an additive defect), tendsto_profile gives EXISTENCE of g(beta) = lim_S f(S, beta S)/S for every beta (Fekete, defect absorbed by shifting), and profile_concave_rat gives CONCAVITY at every rational mixture p/(p+q), realised by splitting the budget S = pk + qk across the two scales.  Extending rational weights to real ones needs one further analytic input (continuity of g, or monotonicity of f in its second argument) and is not formalised.
